keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 32,877 km2 against the infobox 33,843 km2 (1989 census; ratio 1.03): the six Bessarabian counties (29,842 km2) plus the westernmost Moldavian ASSR lands (3,035 km2), drawn as the Natural Earth Moldova with Transnistria. Cliopatria's Republic of Moldova (27,293 km2) begins in 1992 and has no row for the Soviet years, which lie inside its Union of Soviet Socialist Republics shapes; its Kingdom of Romania of 1939 (301,073 km2) holds Bessarabia until 1940. Northern Bukovina, Khotin and Budjak went to the Ukrainian SSR on 2 August 1940.

sources.title: Moldavian Soviet Socialist Republic
sources.note: 2 August 1940 formed; Bessarabia annexed 28 June 1940; Romania recovers Bessarabia in the summer of 1941; Soviet return 1944; sovereignty 23 June 1990; renamed 23 May 1991; independence 27 August 1991; area 33,843 km2 (1989); capital Chisinau.

sources.title: Moldavian Autonomous Soviet Socialist Republic
sources.note: Dissolved 2 August 1940; six Bessarabian counties plus the westernmost 4,118 km2 of the MASSR form the Moldavian SSR.

notes: No Cliopatria row (Cliopatria's Republic of Moldova is 1992 on). The republic is an internal unit of the Soviet Union. The keyframe is the Natural Earth Moldova; the page gives no border change with Ukraine after 1940 and none for the Transnistrian line. The page mentions no Transnistrian secession (1990-1991); not entered. Natural Earth Moldova includes Transnistria, which the 1941-1944 Romanian "Transnistria" governorate occupied; the occupation is recorded over the whole republic. Counterparts: kingdom-of-romania and republic-of-moldova exist (Cliopatria); the Moldavian ASSR dossier is in this batch.
